Nitpicks: The only clear nitpick is minor formatting in the product name (agent wrote “400g e” vs the page showing “400 g e”).

Critical issues: The agent’s output includes several specific facts that are not supported by the provided evidence and appear to be asserted without having visibly reached/recorded those sections. (1) Energy per 100 g (2252 kJ (539 kcal)) is not visible in any screenshot; the nutrition table/per-100-g column is never shown. (2) Sugars per 100 g (56.3 g) is likewise not visible anywhere in the screenshots. (3) The complete English ingredients sentence is not visible in the screenshots. (4) The NOVA marker count (“2 ultra-processing markers”) is not visible; only the classification wording “Ultra-processed foods” is partially visible. These are hard requirements of the task (must report exact displayed per-100-g values/units, exact visible NOVA-card wording and marker count, and complete displayed English ingredients), so unsupported reporting here is a major problem.

What is actually supported: The agent did start from the correct Open Food Facts URL containing the target barcode, and screenshots do show the product as “Nutella – 400 g e” and show “Nutri-Score E.” However, the agent did not provide reliable, evidence-backed completion of the main deliverables (nutrition fields, full ingredients text, and NOVA marker count). From an average user perspective, this means the task is not completed because key requested fields are effectively unverified/likely fabricated rather than recorded from the page as instructed.
